audit_findings.title: New debt’s full-year interest burden is absent from the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.837 million incremental annual pre-tax interest computed at the filed 4.8% rate; approximately $6.207 million after the filed 20.8% effective tax rate, or 3.9% of the $158.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces equity-level OE because debt principal is not deducted and interest must therefore remain fully reflected in forecast earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense totaled $1.8 million in 2026 related to borrowings under our unsecured credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch: the $158.1 million historical anchor includes only $1.763 million of interest, while $200 million at 4.8% implies $9.6 million annually. Correcting the approximately $6.207 million after-tax shortfall would reduce modeled per-share values by about $2.68, $3.08 and $3.54 in the bear, base and bull cases, respectively. The corrected bull value would remain about $87.56 versus the $105.39 market price, so the omission cannot reverse the present valuation conclusion, although the model should still be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios with the contractual amortization schedule, full-year cash interest, facility fees and variable-rate sensitivity; do not add an unobserved Bachan’s earnings run-rate.

audit_findings.title: A $159 million uncommenced lease is outside both the balance-sheet bridge and historical OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $159 million of fixed payments over 15 years; $10.6 million simple annual average, equal to 6.7% of the $158.1 million anchor before replacements, timing and tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Future warehouse rent reduces OE; the lease liability itself need not be separately deducted if all lease expense is retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We have a lease commitment with fixed cash payments totaling approximately $159 million for a lease that had not commenced as of June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment and its absence from historical OE are demonstrated, but the valuation error is not. The filing does not provide the payment schedule, present value, commencement date within fiscal 2027 or costs eliminated when the new warehouse replaces existing capacity. Consequently, the net incremental occupancy cost and its materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the lease schedule and replacement plan, calculate annual net incremental cash occupancy cost, and rerun OE from lease commencement without also deducting the recognized lease liability.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease investment may escape the owner-earnings reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.914 million of fiscal-2026 noncash finance-lease additions and $2.128 million of principal payments, equal to 6.9% and 1.3% of the $158.1 million anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if finance-lease asset amortization is added back through D&A while neither lease principal nor an appropriate productive-asset reinvestment charge is deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: We have finance leases with initial noncancelable lease terms in excess of one year covering the rental of various facilities and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The lease amounts are filed facts, but an omission is not demonstrated because the OE adjustment ledger is absent. The $10.914 million addition cannot automatically be treated as recurring maintenance, and deducting both the asset addition and principal would double count the same investment. The possible error could matter, but the record cannot establish its recurring amount or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to finance-lease amortization, additions and principal; classify maintenance versus growth assets and deduct the economic productive-asset cost exactly once before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Near-term capital spending is above the anchor-year level
audit_findings.magnitude: $90 million planned for fiscal 2027, $12.321 million above fiscal-2026 property additions of $77.679 million and $24.241 million above depreciation of $65.759 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Unavoidable maintenance, replacement, integration or compliance spending would reduce forecast OE or require greater reinvestment to support forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on our current plans and expectations, we believe our capital expenditures for 2027 could total approximately $90 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending plan is forward-looking and therefore is not a demonstrated error in the historical anchor. Its classification is undisclosed: discretionary growth spending would not justify a dollar-for-dollar anchor reduction, whereas unavoidable maintenance or replacement spending could. The $12.321 million increase is 7.8% of the anchor, so subsequent evidence warrants monitoring.
audit_findings.action: Track fiscal-2027 capital guidance and actual spending by maintenance, replacement, integration, compliance and growth categories; rerun OE for the unavoidable recurring portion.

audit_findings.title: Thirty-percent customer exposure lacks purchase commitments
audit_findings.magnitude: $575.681 million of fiscal-2026 sales, or 30% of consolidated sales; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A volume loss, adverse license renewal or weaker terms would reduce revenue, margins, OE and sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We do not have any long-term purchase commitments from Chick-fil-A or such distributors, and we may be unable to continue to sell our products in the same quantities or on the same terms as in the past.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration and absence of long-term purchase commitments are demonstrated, but no customer loss or deterioration is presently recorded. Sales exposure cannot be translated into OE without customer-level contribution margins, contract terms and mitigation capacity. This is a material forward-looking concentration risk rather than a current valuation-input error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Foodservice and licensed-Retail contract durations, termination rights and customer-level contribution margins, then stress-test partial and complete Chick-fil-A reductions with realistic stranded costs.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition costs must not be automatically normalized away in an acquisition-led strategy
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.509 million in fiscal 2026 and $3.781 million in fiscal 2025; the fiscal-2026 amount equals 9.2% of the $158.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing transaction and integration costs raises normalized OE; retaining acquisition-dependent growth without its recurring economic acquisition cost also overstates growth-funded value.
audit_findings.evidence: SG&A expenses in the current year included $14.5 million in incremental expenditures attributed to the Bachan’s acquisition transaction costs in addition to $1.6 million in incremental noncash amortization expense for Bachan’s intangible assets.
audit_findings.explanation: Consecutive acquisition costs and the acquisition-led strategy are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the judged OE series removed these costs or whether scenario growth depends on continued acquisitions. Accordingly, neither an actual error nor its recurring amount is established. If the full fiscal-2026 cost was excluded while acquired growth was credited, the scale could be material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the year-by-year OE adjustment ledger and growth attribution; restore transaction and integration costs whenever modeled growth requires continued M&A, exclude only noncash amortization as appropriate, and rerun.
